terra.problem: Saying nobody in the scene is checking a phone puts a modern detail into the Bible event rather than keeping it in a separate comparison.
The claim that a pillar stands still conflicts with the cited passage, where the pillar of cloud goes before Israel.
The claim that Job came ready to ask goes beyond this passage and needs a supporting reference.
The verse describes shouting for joy, but it does not say there was no fear in the scene.
Giving a guest an address does not match the action of setting a boundary, so the comparison fails the joke logic test.
The toddler comparison is a modern scenario about parents, which the audience rules prohibit.
The LORD asks whether Job has journeyed to the vents; the text does not state that he has not.
Identifying the Jordan as a river is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The LORD asks whether Job has seen the gates; the text does not state that Job has not seen them.
A desert where no one lives does not necessarily mean nobody is present to see the rain.
The questions about knowing in this passage are the LORD's questions to Job, not questions Job is shown asking.
Saying naming all the animals happened overstates Genesis 2:20, which names livestock, birds and beasts of the field.
The explanation implies Cain built the first city. Genesis 4:17 says he built a city, but does not call it the first.
